body:
Probed with `zmx set`:
- Keys and values accept only [a-zA-Z0-9-_.]. Rejections are errors naming the offending part; `path=/tmp/x`, `colon=a:b`, `sp ace=v` and an emoji value are all refused.
- A space inside a value is not an error: `note=hello world` quietly stores `note=hello` and drops the rest. So values are single tokens, and prose in a label is impossible rather than merely discouraged.
- `k=` alone removes the key. Long values are fine (300 chars stored).
- No timestamps and no authors: the last writer wins and nothing records who or when. A stale `state=done` is indistinguishable from a fresh one.
- `zmx get` prints labels sorted by key, ASCII order (uppercase before lowercase); `zmx ls` prints built-ins then labels in the same order. All-lowercase keys keep order predictable.
- Inside a session, `ZMX_SESSION` names it (verified via `run env`), so a program can label itself without being told its name: `zmx set "$ZMX_SESSION" state=blocked`.
title: Labels are tokens, not text, and they are unowned
